newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish hotel chain ORBIS sale seen in late 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish hotel chain ORBIS sale seen in late 1997.

text.p: Poland's state-owned hotel and travel agency chain Orbis SA is likely to start its privatisation late in 1997, the Orbis president said on Monday.
"Being optimistic it should happen in the middle of the year, but being realistic rather late autumn, around October," Maciej Grelowski told Reuters.

Grelowski said about 20 percent of Orbis shares are likely to be sold to a passive investor, but said it had yet to be decided whether the privatisation would start with selling shares hold by the state treasury or by a new issue.
He added the company would prefer a Polish or a foreign financial institution as the passive investor.

Grelowski also said between 30 and 35 percent of shares in Orbis could be earmarked for the Warsaw bourse, 15 percent for employees and five percent for a planned fund to meet claims for property taken under communism.
He added the state treasury took into account earmarking some of Orbis shares for pension funds after the country carries out its social security reform.

Grelowski said a new issue would likely be voted on by the general shareholders meeting planned for June, but said it had yet to be decided whether the issue would be carried out before or after the company enters the bourse.
He said the funds from the issue would be earmarked for modernisation. He added the funds needed for modernisation amounted to 450 million zlotys.
Grelowski said the firm's sales amounted to about 500 million zlotys in 1995 and according to preliminary data to 600 million in 1996.
The firm, which employs about 10,000, had a net profit of about 19 million zlotys and about 28 million in 1996.
